spec_match.rationale: Concepts map the current Editor's Draft while labelling its draft status: presentation enums openid4vp-v1-unsigned/-signed/-multisigned and org-iso-mdoc; issuance enum openid4vci-v1; static DigitalCredential.userAgentAllowsProtocol on the interface object; and distinct get/create request dictionaries carrying { protocol: DOMString, data: object }. Chromium's digital_credential.idl supplies implementation evidence ([CallWith=ScriptState] static; interface gated WebIdentityDigitalCredentials), not normative Web text. Layers remain separate: protocol policy, get versus create, provider/wallet selection, digital-credentials-get/create permissions policies, user mediation, origin binding, and actual disclosure.

interactive.rationale: Real probes and builders: sentinel-based filtering detection (bogus token → false means active), per-protocol allowed/blocked/unknown cells, custom identifier checks, request assembly with pre-flight, and an explicit-click-only send with AbortController, 10s honest timeout, and cancel — no credential request is ever auto-fired.

blurb_alignment.rationale: Index and ledes now match the evidence boundary: ChromeStatus records a deprecation developer trial from 151 and schedules removal at 160 while overall status remains 'Proposed' (updated 2026-06-18). The static method belongs to the DC API where implemented; Chrome 151 is not presented as a universal shipping claim for that method or as proof filtering is active in every session.

edge_cases.rationale: Fixed the stale bare 'openid4vp' identifier everywhere (absent from the current Editor's Draft enums). Parent review separated presentation protocols used by navigator.credentials.get() from issuance-only openid4vci-v1 used by navigator.credentials.create(), added a distinct issuance pattern, and reports draft membership separately from each live browser-policy result. A rejected sentinel is evidence consistent with filtering, not proof of an exhaustive allowlist. Future Chrome 160 behavior is labelled scheduled/proposed, and no protocol result implies wallet acceptance.

references.rationale: All four pages cite chromestatus.com/feature/6492906882990080. All four pages link the Editor's Draft protocols section; the index and migration guide link FedID WG resolution #396; the index also links MDN's DigitalCredential page. The critique distinguishes current draft text, Chromium implementation IDL/runtime gates, and ChromeStatus scheduling.

conformance.rationale: New immutable root suite (this cycle, 8 assertions — 8 JSON entries = 8 rendered rows = 8 reported): interface existence, static typeof and arity, two binding traps (not on navigator.credentials or the prototype), required false for an unregistered grammar-valid token, and boolean results for one presentation and one issuance enum value. Parent review removed generic Credential Management host checks and a vacuous secure-context assertion. No credential request is constructed or fired.

runtime_evidence.rationale: chrome-devtools-mcp on HeadlessChrome/150 (DigitalCredential PRESENT and the static userAgentAllowsProtocol exposed with correct binding — not on prototype, not on navigator.credentials — but protocol filtering inactive: every token, including the sentinel, returns true; verified directly twice after an initial stale-context misread): controls were exercised at 1280×800 and 390×844. Parent review revalidated the revised 390px states: the three-column allowlist initially overflowed to 460px and was fixed to 390px; the issuance identifier reports create context; the new OpenID4VCI tab and Home-key navigation work; the presentation-only builder exposes pending/timeout without inferring chooser or wallet state; zero console errors or failed requests. The rendered suite recount is 7 pass / 1 fail / 0 blocked across exactly 8 rows, with only unknown-token rejection failing under the legacy opaque behavior.

telemetry_health.rationale: Concepts emit showcaseTelemetry.assert events per branch (dc-allows-probed, dc-custom-check, dc-builder-loaded, dc-get-resolved/rejected-cleanly/timed-out/cancelled, dc-migration-loaded/analyzed); telemetry POSTs returned 202 during validation.

design_system.rationale: CSS variables throughout, button background+color pairs, focus-visible styles, no static-card pattern; edits were list/copy/example level and preserve layout.

accessibility.rationale: role=status/aria-live on banners, verdicts, and send results; labelled inputs; the three migration tabs implement the full ARIA tabs pattern (aria-selected, roving tabindex, arrow/Home/End keys); sr-only labels on text inputs.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Matrix pass including post-interaction states: K3 tested all four pages at 1280×800 and 390×844. Parent review caught a new 460px allowlist overflow after adding the context column, fixed it with a fixed-layout wrapping table, and remeasured 390px exactly. Revised migration tab/analyzer and builder pending/timeout states also remain at 390px.

openQuestions.title: Verify live filtering behavior and the exact registered allowlist on a DigitalCredentialsProtocolFilter-enabled build
openQuestions.detail: This build (HeadlessChrome/150, secure localhost context) exposes the Digital Credentials API and the static userAgentAllowsProtocol but NOT the filtering gate: every protocol — registered or bogus — returns true (the legacy opaque pipeline), which the demos report honestly as 'filtering not active yet'. On a build with the DigitalCredentialsProtocolFilter runtime feature on (dev trial from Chrome 151), verify: sentinel rejected, which identifiers the UA actually allows (the current Editor's Draft enums list openid4vp-v1-unsigned/-signed/-multisigned + org-iso-mdoc for presentation and openid4vci-v1 for issuance; Chromium's concrete policy may differ during the trial — the stale bare 'openid4vp' currently still returns true here and must not be presented as part of those enums), and the digital-credentials-get permissions-policy behavior for cross-origin embedding. Update the tables/banners if the concrete list diverges.

guidanceConsulted.query: accessible live region announcements for dynamic probe/status results after button activation
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Announce dynamic state through live regions tied to the activating control; give interactive tabs the full ARIA tabs pattern.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Verified applied: banners/verdicts/send-results are role=status aria-live; the migration tabs carry aria-selected + roving tabindex + arrow/Home/End keyboard support (exercised live).

guidanceConsulted.query: credential request flows that require explicit user mediation and never auto-fire identity requests
guidanceConsulted.recommendation: Sensitive account/credential operations must be explicitly user-initiated with clear context; never fire them automatically or fake their outcomes.
guidanceConsulted.appliedOrException: Applied strictly: navigator.credentials.get() fires only on an explicit button click, with abort, user cancel, and an honest 10s no-wallet timeout; no credential request is auto-issued anywhere in the family.
guidanceConsulted.evidence: chrome-devtools-mcp interaction log — zero credential requests outside the explicit send attempt

summary: Source-review of the Protocol-filtering family against the current Digital Credentials Editor's Draft (separate presentation and issuance enums; static userAgentAllowsProtocol; distinct get/create request dictionaries), Chromium implementation IDL/runtime gates, and direct ChromeStatus evidence (updated 2026-06-18: deprecation developer trial 151, scheduled removal 160, overall 'Proposed'). Fixed stale bare openid4vp identifiers and universal shipping language. Parent review further separated presentation get from issuance create, added an OpenID4VCI issuance pattern, removed provider/wallet inferences, treated sentinel detection as evidence rather than exhaustive proof, and made future removal language explicitly scheduled/proposed. Added the immutable 8-assertion root suite with binding, arity, unknown-token rejection, and separate presentation/issuance return contracts. Missing-suite denominator 7→6 expected (792/798).
